GAUSSIAN RIGIDITY FOR INFINITE EXCHANGEABLE SEQUENCES

                                                                           B Y Y USHU Z HENG1,a AND Q I Z HOU2,b
                                                    1 Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, a yszheng666@gmail.com

                                                                2 School of Mathematical Sciences, Soochow University, b zhouqi@suda.edu.cn


                                                                 We prove a Gaussian rigidity theorem for infinite exchangeable se-
                                                            quences of real-valued random variables: the joint Gaussianity of a single
                                                            pair of entries already forces the entire sequence to be a Gaussian process.
                                                            This settles a conjecture raised by Newman (2026). The main analytic ingre-




arXiv:2606.25976v1 [math.PR] 24 Jun 2026
                                                            dient in the proof is Hardy’s uncertainty principle. We also obtain a finite-
                                                            dimensional vector-valued extension.


                                               1. Introduction. Gaussian processes are defined by their finite-dimensional distribu-
                                           tions, so checking Gaussianity is usually a global task. A natural question is whether, un-
                                           der suitable structural assumptions, this global property can be detected from much smaller
                                           pieces of the process. The present paper proves such a result for infinite exchangeable se-
                                           quences: the joint Gaussianity of one pair of distinct coordinates already forces the whole
                                           sequence to be a Gaussian process.
